messages:
Maya: FYI ALB in us-west-2 just started deregistering ~30 edge targets from the edge-gpu pool, all showing readiness failure within ~60s. Not sure if this is infra or app. Anyone?
Sam: seeing it too, started ~10:12 UTC. ALB access logs show requests succeeding to ELB but 504 from targets. Targets subsequently deregistered.
deploy-bot: ALERT: target.deregistered count=29 for arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:targetgroup/edge-tg (reason=unhealthy)
Maya: quick check — curl from node to pod IP -> `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://10.1.4.22:8080/readiness` returns 200 consistently. So app readiness seems fine when hit locally.
Sam: pasted small ALB snippet:
Sam: ```2026-03-18T10:11:58.000Z alb 1.2.3.4:443 10.0.1.23:8080 0.002 0.350 0.000 504 200 "GET /readiness HTTP/1.1" ...```
Cleo: hmm 0.350s backend time then 504 — could be a TCP idle/reset during healthcheck handshake. We did change ip-masq rule deployment last night.
Toni: I saw kube-proxy restart events around the same window on a few nodes. When kube-proxy restarts we briefly remove some iptables nat rules — that can change SNAT mappings.
Alex: ALB healthchecks are stateless HTTP requests but they open a new TCP connection each time. If SNAT mapping flips mid-flow the backend might send response to old source and ELB times out.
Maya: reproduced quickly: restart kube-proxy on node hosting some targets; node-local curl still works, but ALB->target times out and target goes Unhealthy after 2 fails.
Sam: quick diagnostic commands we ran:
Sam: ```# on node
sudo systemctl restart kube-proxy
sudo iptables -t nat -S | grep MASQUERADE || true
# on control plane
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn ...
```
Cleo: @netops (cc) can you confirm NAT gateway idle timeout? If the NAT gateway closes outbound mapping quickly, and ip-masq rules briefly remove/recreate SNAT, that could cause probe jitter.
deploy-bot: INFO: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-01 — ALB target health flapping in us-west-2-edge cluster
Toni: Workaround applied: pinned kube-proxy rollout paused and we reverted the ip-masq change to previous rule set. Targets re-registered within ~2 minutes. :thumbsup:
Alex: Longer-term: we should ensure ip-masq changes are applied atomically and make kube-proxy restarts draining-friendly for ALB healthchecks (e.g., set `externalTrafficPolicy` / enable source IP preservation where possible). Also check conntrack reuse settings.
Maya: sounds good. I'll file a follow-up RFC and include a runbook: detection query (CloudWatch/alb logs), immediate rollback steps, and a kube-proxy restart checklist.
Cleo: I'll own the RFC and add a test that simulates kube-proxy restart during heavy ALB healthcheck.
Sam: adding postmortem notes to INC-2026-0318-01.
Maya: thanks — marking this thread for handoff to NetOps and Eng Infra.
Alex: one more note — consider increasing ALB healthcheck interval/threshold for this target group while we harden config so we avoid noisy evictions.
Toni: +1, filed quick config change PR to change healthy threshold from 2 -> 3 for edge-tg (will monitor).
Cleo: assigning follow-ups in the incident ticket. :ok_hand:
